Package chess.pieces

Class Piece

java.lang.Object
chess.pieces.Piece
Direct Known Subclasses:
Bishop, King, Knight, Pawn, Queen, Rook
public abstract class Piece extends Object
The superclass for all six chess pieces.

Every piece has a color and a position, prints as a two-letter symbol such as wR, and can move to a new square. Each subclass decides where it can move by overriding possibleMoves(Board).

The sliding pieces (rook, bishop and queen) share the slide(Board, int[][]) helper, which walks in straight lines until it reaches the edge of the board or another piece.

  • Method Details

    • possibleMoves

      public abstract List<Position> possibleMoves(Board board)
      Returns every square this piece could move to from its current position. Each subclass overrides this with its own movement rules.

      The result follows the piece's movement pattern, path blocking and captures. It does not check whether a move leaves the king in check.

      Parameters:
      board - the current board, used to see which squares are occupied
      Returns:
      a list of destination squares, empty if the piece can't move

      public boolean isPromotable()

    • slide

      protected List<Position> slide(Board board, int[][] directions)
      Collects the squares reached by sliding in each given direction. In each direction it keeps stepping over empty squares and stops when it reaches the edge of the board or another piece. An enemy piece's square is included (a capture); a friendly piece's square is not.
      Parameters:
      board - the current board
      directions - pairs of {rowChange, colChange}, such as {-1, 0} for up
      Returns:
      all reachable squares in those directions

    • step

      protected List<Position> step(Board board, int[][] offsets)
      Collects the squares reached by a single hop with each given offset. A square is included if it is on the board and is empty or holds an enemy piece. Used by pieces that move exactly once, like the knight and king.
      Parameters:
      board - the current board
      offsets - pairs of {rowChange, colChange}, such as {-2, 1}
      Returns:
      all squares the piece can land on with those offsets
